Replace the minimal implementation of utc_timestamp with a correct implementation that parses an ISO 8601 datetime string, ensures the timezone is explicit (accepting Z), and returns the integer Unix seconds in UTC; reject naive datetimes with ValueError.
Full access (host permissions)
Original file will be saved for undo.
Checkpoint: 8cb69587-8d18-4e28-ba73-f728a7ae6737
--- a/solution.py
+++ b/solution.py
@@ -1 +1,12 @@
-def utc_timestamp(text):return 0
+def utc_timestamp(text):
+    """Return the integer Unix seconds for ``text`` in UTC.
+
+    ``text`` must be an ISO 8601 datetime string with an explicit timezone,
+    accepting ``Z``. Naive datetimes are rejected with a ``ValueError``.
+    """
+    from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
+    if dt.tzinfo is None or dt.tzinfo.utcoffset(dt) is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"'{text}' is not a valid timezone-aware datetime")
+    return dt.timestamp()
